studies.title: The One Who Slinks Away
studies.meaning: Three names of God open the surah, in a descending order the commentators note: Lord, King, God, moving from care to authority to worship. Then one danger, described in three ways. It whispers, it withdraws when God is remembered, and it works inside the chests. The final line widens it: the whisperer may be unseen or may be a person, and the surah gives no way to tell which.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan by the tradition this collection follows, though the classical authorities differ, and it is paired throughout with the surah before it. No occasion is reported separately for this one. It is the last chapter of the Quran, and it closes the Book on a request rather than on a statement, addressed by a human being to the Lord of human beings.

keyTerms.note: An intensive from a verb meaning to retreat and hide, used of an animal that withdraws when noticed. The name describes not an attack but a retreat, so the thing is identified by what it does when caught.
An onomatopoeic form imitating a faint repeated sound, used of jewellery rustling. It names the noise rather than the speaker, so what is described is the quality of the suggestion, not its source.
The word repeats five times in six short lines, which is an unusual density even in a chapter this short. It appears in the three names of God and again as the place the whispering happens.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Whispering had a specific social meaning in Arabia. It was how a man's reputation was undone, how a deal was quietly poisoned, and how a raid was arranged; the Quran addresses private conferences elsewhere as a serious matter. So the image at the end of the Book is not exotic. It names something a listener had experienced at a market or in a courtyard.
studies.didYouKnow: The last word of the Quran is the word for people, and it is the same word that fills the surah. The Book that opens by praising the Lord of all the worlds ends by naming the Lord of human beings, and the final danger it warns about may be a human one. The scale narrows all the way down at the close.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The harm named here is different in kind from the one in the surah before. Nothing is done to you; something is suggested, and the suggestion arrives in the one place you would call yourself. That makes the danger indistinguishable from your own thinking, which is why three names of God are stacked at the front: what is needed is not protection from an attacker but a way to tell whose voice you are hearing.

crossReferences.why: Forms the other half of the pair, listing dangers that arrive from outside a person rather than inside.
Uses the same verb for whispering, this time of the soul itself, and says the whisper is already known.
Gives the practice this surah supplies the words for, and describes the clarity that follows it.

studies.applyIt: The next time a thought arrives that makes you smaller, say this surah before you argue with it. Do not analyse where it came from. The word for the whisperer means the one that withdraws when noticed, so the practical instruction is simply to notice it out loud, and the surah gives you the sentence for doing that.
